summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Yasuhiro Ueno completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004) and held a commissioned researcher post at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) studied Buddhist studies at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as associate professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and professor at Koyasan University (~1977–2000), where he taught Takaaki Mori.

Indologist Yasuke Ikari studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1968–1973). He served as associate professor at Kindai University and National Museum of Ethnology, and as professor at Kyoto University (1989).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Yasuko Kojima held posts as lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

A scholar of religious studies and Indology, Yasumasa Sekine studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. His main posts included Japan Women's University (professor, ~1998–2017) and Kwansei Gakuin University (professor, ~2017–2020).

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied at Göttingen. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1987, 1995–1999).

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1987–1992). He served as professor (from 2016) and dean of letters (2023–2025) at Kyoto University.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Yasuo Goto served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and part-time lecturer (attested 2006) at Ryukoku University, as well as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1993–2004) and held a post at Kyoto University (~2004).

Yasuo Matsunami (1946–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who studied under Ryukai Mano and pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995–2006).
Yasuo Sano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyo Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Research Association.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, studying under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Osaka University (1975) and the University of Tsukuba (1981–1989).

Yasuro Abe works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied at Wako and Otani universities. He served as professor at Nagoya University (1998; emeritus 2000–2019) and Ryukoku University (2019).

Yasusaburo Sakaki (1870–1929) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1895–1899). He taught Gikyo Ito and held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyushu University (~1906–1928).

Yasutaka Muroya is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as a project research associate at the University of Vienna and University of Leipzig, and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Yasutoshi Murakami, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Tohoku University. He held academic posts at Yamaguchi University (~1976–2007) and Koyasan University (~2007–2013).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yeshe Thubten (1935–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, and Zong Rinpoche. He taught at the University of California, Santa Cruz (1977–1978).
Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) was a Tibetology scholar who studied at Chakpori Medical College under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961 and served as its director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2001).
